title: Specification-Gaming in the Wild: Auditing METR-Style Task Transcripts for Shortcut Exploits

original_idea.body:
# Specification-Gaming in the Wild: Auditing METR-Style Task Transcripts for Shortcut Exploits

**Problem:** Reward-hacking benchmarks show agents exploit task loopholes, but a grounded characterization of which task-design features invite shortcut exploitation (weak verifier, ambiguous success criterion, gameable metric) on open task suites is lacking.

**Direction:** Use a small open agentic task suite (e.g. selected METR-style tasks or a public reward-hacking benchmark) and run an open model, logging full transcripts. Manually code each transcript for whether the agent gamed the verifier vs. genuinely solved the task, then correlate gaming with task features (verifier strictness, metric type, presence of a trivially-satisfying output). Output a checklist of task-design smells that invite gaming.

**Why it matters:** Produces practical, reusable guidance for designing gaming-resistant agentic evals — directly improving the nascent evaluation infrastructure the subfield depends on. Uses open task suites and a single GPU; the analysis itself is valuable independent of any lab.

**Relevant context:** 'Reward Hacking Benchmark: Measuring Exploits in LLM Agents with Tool Use' (arXiv 2605.02964); METR open task suites (subfield source code availability). Anthropic reward-hacking work shows generalization from exploits to misalignment.
